Welcome to Glebe Farm School
Glebe Farm School is an exciting, brand new fossil-free new build all-through school in the parish of Wavendon in the South East of Milton Keynes, which welcomed its first pupils in September 2022.
A place of learning and engagement for pupils and the community, the provision of an innovative, excellent and broad education for 1530 pupils from ages 4 to 16 (with an additional 39 place nursery setting) is at the heart of the vision for Glebe Farm School.

Drama
The Glebe Farm Drama Department strives to nurture confident, creative and thoughtful learners. It is our belief that the practice of Drama enables students to explore a wide range performance texts, stimuli and career opportunities withing the arts. Our curriculum offers pupils a chance to explore different contexts and a varied and dynamic set of themes, along with supporting students with subjects such as English, History and Science through a variation of cross-curricular links. Pupils are set ambitious devising, knowledge and performance goals that encourage them to take risks and consider the world in a more perceptive way.
Throughout the curriculum, pupils will navigate a range of themes and texts that should motivate and inspire them to respond creatively. The knowledge and skills that the pupils develop will support them in becoming considerate, dedicated and enigmatic performers, whilst ensuring that students are perceived as personable and confident young people.
Communication is at the heart of Drama. We will encourage learners to consider how their body-language, movement, vocality and voice can impact how we communicate. Pupils will explore performing monologues, duologues and group performances, building a strong sense of belonging and collaboration. It is the aim of the Drama department to support pupils to become upstanding, thoughtful members of their community.

SALs & Guinness Partnership
Glebe Farm School are proud to work in partnership with SALS Shoes and The Guinness Partnership to support our families facing financial crisis.
Together we are able to offer school shoes and uniform to those we are working with. We provide a complete shop experience from having your feet measured, trying on shoes & uniform, checking yourself out in the mirror to see how ‘cool’ you look and taking them home in a box/bag.

"Kidz Zone“ is open to all children in Reception to Year 7 attending Glebe Farm School. At ‘Kidz Zone’ we provide a fun, active, safe environment for children, under the care of qualified staff.

Breakfast Club 7:30am – 8:15am
The breakfast club runs from 7:30am – 8:45am, Monday – Friday. Children have a choice of indoor activities each day. Breakfast is included in the form of cereals, toast and juice. The cost is £5.85 per session from 7:30am or £4.25 per session from 8:00am.
After School Club 3:30pm - 6:00pm

Construction - Based around our weekly theme! + Free Play

The ‘Active Hour’ is open to all children at the school not just children who need to attend for childcare purposes; it’s a great opportunity for children to socialise, have fun and learn new skills with friends!

Art
Our art curriculum is driven by a commitment to fostering ambition, cultivating a sense of belonging, and nurturing creativity in every learner. We believe that the arts provide a powerful platform for learners to express themselves, explore new ideas, and challenge conventional boundaries. Through the process of creating, learners develop confidence in their abilities and a sense of ownership over their work, encouraging them to set high personal goals and strive for excellence. We aim to create an environment where every learner feels they belong, where their unique perspectives are valued and celebrated, and where collaboration is encouraged as a means of strengthening community and artistic expression.
Our curriculum also integrates key contemporary issues, including climate change and sustainability, into the creative process. By exploring these global challenges through the lens of art, learners are invited to reflect on their role in the world and consider how creative practices can advocate for change; encouraging them to think critically about their environmental footprint and to envision a more sustainable future.
Engagement with the creative process is at the heart of our curriculum. We recognise that true learning in the arts stems from a desire to create, a passion that fuels curiosity and growth. Our approach fosters an environment where learners are inspired not only by the technical aspects of art-making but also by the joy of experimentation and discovery. By encouraging risk-taking, exploring diverse media, and embracing both successes and failures, we ensure that learners find personal meaning in their creative work. As they progress through the curriculum, learners are empowered to enjoy the journey of creation, with the understanding that the process itself holds value, and that their creativity is a vital and transformative force in their lives.

Computing
Computing Curriculum Intent
The computing curriculum at Glebe Farm School is built upon the principles of digital literacy, computer science and information technology. Students will engage with an ambitious curriculum, fostering a deep understanding of computer science principles, information, and computation. Students learn how digital systems operate and apply this knowledge through problem-solving and computational thinking. This foundation empowers students to harness digital technologies to create innovative solutions, systems, and diverse content.
By integrating computing with mathematics, science, and design technology, the curriculum provides valuable insights into both natural and artificial systems. It ensures students become digitally literate, enabling them to express themselves creatively and develop their ideas through information and communication technology. This approach prepares students for the future workplace and helps them become active participants in a 21st-century digital world, creating a sense of belonging and encouraging creativity.

English
English Curriculum Intent
The Glebe Farm English Department endeavours to create articulate, creative and reflective learners. We believe the study of English supports pupils to develop socially, emotionally, culturally and intellectually through their exploration of our rich heritage of stories to inform our understanding of the world around us. Our thematic curriculum guides pupils through the rich historical and cultural significance of the tradition of storytelling and the enduring power of language: from the origins of sense making stories to the power of language today in our fast-paced, diverse world. A rich and ambitious variety of texts exposes pupils to the evolution, purpose and significance of storytelling from a range of forms, genres and periods.
Our engaging and varied choice of texts inspire and promote a love and appreciation of reading for pleasure. Knowledge intersperses with skill, to support pupils to become insightful, critical readers and controlled, creative writers. Our thematic curriculum develops conceptual schemas that encourages students to see patterns, appreciate deep layers of meaning and make connections across literature, language and media. Engaging and relevant thematic texts inspire learners to develop a command of writing in a range of forms and genres.
We recognise the ability to communicate effectively, confidently and with clarity is crucial in school and beyond. Opportunities are created for learners to develop a strong command of the spoken word to discuss and debate ideas in a safe and inclusive environment; we firmly believe in these opportunities to build confidence and a sense of belonging. We guide pupils to become confident, articulate and sophisticated communicators preparing our learners to become successful, valuable and socially responsible citizens.

N.B. For the Academic year 24/25 summer term unit has changed from Ecosystems to Population.
Why this?
This concept question is ideal because it encourages students to explore both the patterns and processes of population change, such as growth, decline, migration, and demographic transitions. It also pushes them to consider the impacts of these changes on people, places, and the planet—making links to development, urbanisation, resource use, and global inequality. The question is open-ended and thought-provoking, allowing for deep enquiry, case study exploration, and critical thinking. It connects local and global perspectives, helping students understand why population is a key issue in today’s world and in the future.
Why now?
Teaching population in Year 9 is especially important now because the world is experiencing rapid and uneven demographic changes that will shape the future of societies, economies, and the environment. From ageing populations in developed countries to youthful populations in developing regions, students need to understand these dynamics to make sense of global challenges like migration, urbanisation, and climate change. As young people becoming global citizens, it's crucial they grasp how population pressures affect resources, health care, housing, and employment—and how governments and communities are responding. This knowledge is vital in a world where understanding people and places is key to building a sustainable future.

History
History Curriculum Intent
The Glebe Farm History Department aims to inspire curiosity and a deep appreciation for the past, helping students develop a strong sense of belonging through their understanding of history at local, national, and global levels. By exploring the experiences of different people and societies across time, students will gain a broader perspective on the world, fostering empathy, respect, and a strong awareness of identity.
Our ambitious and chronologically structured curriculum is designed to help students see the connections between historical events and their lasting impact on the modern world. By engaging with a wide range of sources, interpretations, and case studies, pupils will develop the ability to question, analyse, and think critically about the past.
Teaching is approached creatively, using a variety of methods such as enquiry-based learning, role play, debate, storytelling, and the exploration of historical artefacts and sources. This ensures that students of all abilities and learning styles can engage with history in a meaningful way. Through dynamic and interactive lessons, we encourage students to develop a passion for historical study, allowing them to explore the past in ways that are both analytical and imaginative.
Literacy is at the heart of our curriculum, with a focus on developing students’ historical vocabulary, enhancing their reading skills, and refining their academic writing. Pupils engage with a wide range of historical texts, sources, and interpretations, improving their ability to read critically, extract key information, and form their own reasoned arguments. Writing is developed through structured opportunities to explain, evaluate, and construct well-supported arguments, ensuring that students can express their ideas clearly and confidently in both written and spoken forms.
Through the study of history, students gain insight into Britain’s diverse heritage, its evolving role within Europe and the Commonwealth, and the wider forces that have shaped our society. The curriculum actively promotes British values, including democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance. By examining key moments in history, students develop an understanding of how these values have been challenged and upheld over time, helping them become informed and responsible citizens.
Whether students continue with history beyond Year 9 or not, they will leave with the knowledge and skills to understand the world around them, engage in informed discussions, and appreciate the complexity of historical narratives. Our goal is to equip students with the confidence to question, challenge, and contribute to the ongoing story of our shared past, using a variety of historical approaches and perspectives to develop critical, engaged, and thoughtful learners.

Maths
The Glebe Farm School all-through maths curriculum endeavours to cultivate ambitious, creative learners with a strong sense of belonging, fostering a lifelong love of learning and preparing them to be successful citizens.
Ambition in our maths curriculum means providing a high-quality mathematical education that encourages the unique potential of each learner. We aim to inspire a lifelong love of learning in mathematics that develops reasoning and problem-solving skills. Our rigorous curriculum provides a range of opportunities to meet the needs of individual learners throughout the school, ensuring a deep and secure understanding of mathematical concepts.
We strive to create a strong sense of belonging within mathematics by engaging learners in collaborative problem-solving and discussions, ensuring they develop as responsible, active participants in their mathematical learning journey. We aim to provide opportunities for learners to work collaboratively, sharing different mathematical strategies, and understanding various approaches to problem-solving. All learners from Early Years Foundation Stage to GCSE, are encouraged to take part in activities which engage them as citizens and empower them to recognise both the value and their own potential in applying mathematical concepts to real-world scenarios and contributing to their community.
Creativity is fostered within mathematics by encouraging children to take risks, explore different methods, and think critically to solve problems. Our progressive and sequential spiral curriculum will provide learners with opportunities to develop logical and methodical thinking enabling them to solve a wide range of mathematical problems with confidence and fluency. While the curriculum focuses on mathematical content and skills, the encouragement of creative thinking and problem-solving permeates all areas, empowering learners to become innovators and critical thinkers who can approach challenges with confidence.
This all-through spiral curriculum spanning from Early Years Foundation Stage to GCSE, ensures that fundamental concepts are revisited and deepened as learners progress through the school. This all-through approach allows for a seamless transition between the Key Stages ensuring a cohesive educational journey.

Religious Education
Our Religious Studies course offers the opportunity to engage with a range of world views through a curriculum that is Ambitious and knowledge rich and enables learners to understand themselves within the complex multi-religious and multi-secular world we live in. We explore key questions and concepts through the lenses of the three academic disciplines - Theology, Philosophy and Social Sciences and this, combined with a focus on religious literacy, means that learners will have the ability to hold balanced and well-informed conversations about religion and worldviews.
Through offering a curriculum that is open, enquiring and exploratory, we are promoting mutual respect and acceptance amongst our learners. This allows for a safe space to explore personal beliefs, as well as the beliefs of others in our diverse community and as a result creates a sense of Belonging and reflects the British values. From this, learners may also have a deeper understanding of their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development and how they have come to form their own Worldview. We aim to provide a varied and enriching curriculum where students not only gain powerful knowledge and skills, but can also feed their curiosity through experience, investigation, Creativity, cultural expression and enquiry.

Science
Science Curriculum Intent
At Glebe Farm, our Science Department is committed to fostering a culture of Ambition, Belonging, and Creativity, inspiring students to explore the wonders of the natural world and develop a deep understanding of scientific principles. Our curriculum is designed to nurture curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills through engaging, hands-on learning experiences.
We aim to empower students with the knowledge and skills necessary to excel in science and beyond. By challenging them to think analytically and apply scientific concepts to real-world problems, we encourage high aspirations and a passion for discovery. Our students are supported to achieve their full potential, preparing them for future careers in STEM and other fields.
Science is for everyone. We cultivate an inclusive learning environment where all students feel valued and confident in their scientific abilities. Through collaboration and teamwork, we promote respect for diverse perspectives, fostering a strong sense of community and shared responsibility in scientific exploration.
Innovation is at the heart of scientific progress. Our curriculum encourages students to think creatively, design experiments, and explore new ideas. By integrating cutting-edge technology and inquiry-based learning, we inspire students to question, investigate, and develop original solutions to complex challenges. We embrace modern technology to enhance scientific learning. Technology enables us to bring science to life, providing dynamic and immersive learning experiences.
Understanding and protecting our planet is a key priority. We embed sustainability throughout our curriculum, teaching students about environmental responsibility and the impact of science on the world. Through hands-on practical science, students engage in experiments that reinforce theoretical knowledge, making learning both meaningful and memorable.
By instilling a love for science and a commitment to lifelong learning, we prepare our students to be informed, responsible, and innovative citizens, ready to shape the future through scientific inquiry and discovery.
